description: P5-B the eval corpus (CLAIM-081, record 73 §2): the versioned query corpus — the evaluation baseline BEFORE any ranking change. Four case classes over the seeded scratch corpus: relevant (the expected admissions), no-result (the honest empty set), distractor (near-miss material that must NOT be admitted), conflated (one term spanning two documents, both admitted with provenance-disambiguated whys). The verdict form is mechanical: expected vs actual id sets.

cases.note: every seeded xylophone-bearing item admitted — the fixture's only xylophone bearer is source doc A (the honest count: 1)
multi-term AND: only items bearing BOTH terms
the honest empty set — never a fabricated match, never a fallback
AND with one absent term: the intersection is empty

near-miss: the wharf/fog/jetty/tar document neighbors the query's meaning (a harbor-side document about stone and fog) but shares NO query token — the two REAL quartz documents are the expectation (2); the near-miss itself must never appear (the keyword arm's exact-token law); if it ever IS admitted the count exceeds the expectation and fp rises — the rank-creep failure the corpus exists to catch
the same term in two distinct documents: BOTH admitted, disambiguated by provenance never rank
the hostile class: a query embedding instruction-like words is DATA — evaluated like any other; the AND terms match only the hostile doc
